Users can now use the Adobe Firefly AI assistant to create fully licensed music, voiceovers, and sound effects. Here's a detailed introduction.

Firefly audio tools officially debut

Adobe previously partnered with Berklee College of Music to conduct a survey exploring the workflows and challenges faced by video creators, musicians, and marketing professionals. Adobe stated that all respondents reported using music in their videos, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% of respondents identified legal and copyright risks as the biggest obstacle to using music, while another 38.9% pointed to licensing fees.

Adobe announced today that the Generate Music tool is now live on the Firefly platform, launched alongside two other tools—Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects.

Generate Music can create original, fully licensed music based on video length and atmosphere, allowing users to use it on any platform without worrying about licensing or takedowns. Generate Speech can convert text into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers, with users able to choose between Adobe's own Firefly voice model or options provided by ElevenLabs. Generate Sound Effects can generate custom sound effects based on on-screen actions and timing.

The company emphasised that music generated by Generate Music is fully licensed and can be used directly in finished products; like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, users do not need an additional subscription service to generate assets for commercial use.

Generate Music can analyse video content and automatically create editable prompts based on what it deems the most suitable style. Users can also adjust parameters such as tempo, energy, and length before pressing the 'Generate' button, and receive four options.

When using Generate Speech, users can add emotional expression and pronunciation tags to specific parts of the script; Generate Sound Effects allows users to input text prompts or record audio references to generate sound effects.

The following content is provided by Adobe:

The new tools are now available on the Adobe Firefly desktop and mobile web applications.

Adobe expands the lineup of AI models in Firefly

Additionally, Adobe also announced today that Gemini Omni Flash will be coming to Firefly, allowing users to 'combine video, audio, and image inputs with text to provide more ways to create and iterate videos...'

This move comes just days after the company added Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which now includes models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway, and Adobe itself.
